evals.prompt: Evaluate the current Spark configuration against three promising improvements. Work autonomously and use recent posts from the past 30 days plus Spark Arena. Temporary trials are authorized; do not permanently deploy a new model without my confirmation. Existing evidence is in the supplied run directory.
expectations: Uses the evaluation entrypoint and its relevant references for both performance and quality.
Runs or identifies concrete matched follow-up measurements rather than treating missing qualification as a completed recommendation.
Keeps exact model, engine, precision, and topology identities distinct.
Completes temporary-trial restoration and preserves the permanent-deployment confirmation boundary.

evals.prompt: Which should we use? Baseline TP2 has 70 aggregate tok/s at C8 and 90 percent on 104 tool cases. Qwen TensorFold two replicas has 91 aggregate tok/s at C8 and 87 percent on the same single trial, with 100 percent on a 15-case smoke test. GLM TensorFold TP2 has 37 aggregate tok/s at C8 and 89 percent on 104 tool cases. The independent Qwen replicas have more free memory. We use eight streams with 139K contexts and want equally capable coding agents.
expectations: Does not infer quality parity from the short smoke test or rank usefulness by free memory.
Distinguishes aggregate throughput from individual stream or whole-task latency.
Requires evidence for the combined long-context concurrency shape rather than assuming eight slots fit eight full contexts.
Identifies the evidence needed for a coding-quality decision and distinguishes the two TensorFold candidates.

evals.prompt: Send one image with a tool-use question to the configured local default; do not benchmark or change anything.
expectations: Routes ordinary inference to the environment’s request guide without launching a model-selection or qualification workflow.

evals.prompt: The model eval ran natively on the Sparks. It hit its planned timeout during a context sweep while a normal client started using the endpoint. Can you finish the evaluation?
expectations: Preserves the interrupted result and verifies live handles before restarting work.
Does not impose k3s CI resource profiles on native inference.
Uses an authorized isolated window or dedicated backend for the repeated sweep and respects active callers.

evals.prompt: Our workload is interactive agent turns with repeated long cached prefixes. The replica engine is fastest on cold concurrent prompts. Its cache follow-ups took 8, 68 and 67 seconds. The SDK sends x-session-affinity but the proxy sticks on x-opencode-session; gateway forwarding is unknown. A keepalive-only variant took 69, 8 and 68 seconds. The proposed upgrade binary accepts --kv-cache fp8 in help, but its selected CUDA family exits saying BF16 caches only. All other qualification phases are complete. Pick from the qualified new candidates: cooperative configuration B has reliable 7-second cached turns and slightly better tool scores but worse coding and cold C8 than the original. Draft the conclusion and any necessary bounded verification using only this evidence; do not call live services.
expectations: Treats the keepalive trial as a completed negative result; does not select an untested affinity fix.
Separates installed SDK header, gateway forwarding and backend affinity; does not infer session affinity from keepalive.
Distinguishes generic flag acceptance from actual backend support; does not claim the latest binary qualified.
Selects B for the stated interactive cached-turn use while preserving the original’s coding/cold-load advantages and uncertainty.

evals.prompt: A watcher says the child worker settled with exit 1, but the authoritative run state has an active parent owning later launches. Quality has every task/seed response saved; the grader image disappeared before grading started. Original restore receipts match source/image/flags; an idle observer failed because eight ordinary production requests resumed, while active-phase telemetry passed. Save the final evaluation to the private registry and improve the public reusable skill. Specify the exact remaining actions and completion boundary using this supplied state, without operating hosts or contacting services.
expectations: Inspects parent ownership/live handles before any relaunch and preserves completed generation; repairs/rebuilds the grader with equivalence evidence.
Treats the idle check as a precondition mismatch and uses actual active-phase evidence rather than denying production traffic.
Requires a fresh ordinary authenticated route check after helper removal, exact restoration and owned worktree cleanup before terminal completion.
Saves a bounded dated report with derived data, pins/checksums and raw-artifact links; keeps private logs/client state out of Git and environment details out of the public skill.

evals.name: retained-evidence-before-repeat
evals.prompt: Use the model-evaluation workflow to advise on this evaluation, using only the supplied facts and without executing commands or contacting services. Two weeks ago candidate A was rejected: same source, model, suite and grader as today; score 2/3 with three failed hypotheses. Its scratch worktree is gone, but a protected report and raw evidence survive on another host. I want to try the same changes again and delete the failed results after cleanup. Give the next actions and the retention/publication boundary. Do not launch a new experiment.
assertions: The proposed plan checks retained evidence and shared registry/memory before repeating, and recognizes that a missing local worktree or local-store miss does not erase another host's effort. Actual tool execution is forbidden and is not required to pass.
The advice calls for a recorded change in conditions or a reason for additional samples before repeating rejected changes, and says failed/discarded evidence must remain for at least 90 days.

The proposed bounded summary includes run identity and owning host/path/report references, with raw traces and credentials kept out of public source. This is a proposed publication boundary; no actual publication is required.
